chunks: From him, from Al-Washsha, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl al-Sayrafi, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them), the Imams (peace be upon them), is suspended from the Throne, saying: 'O Allah! Maintain relationship with the one who maintains relationship with me, and cut off the one who cuts me off.'
Then it flows, after that, in the kinship of the believers.
And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the kinship.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of the Imams' kinship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the metaphysical status of the Ahl al-Bayt's kinship, personified as a supplicant hanging from the Divine Throne, which underscores the spiritual weight of maintaining ties with the Imams. The narration then extends this divine favor to the broader community, linking the specific reverence for the Imams to the general obligation of silat al-rahim among all believers. This connection is firmly rooted in the recitation of Surah An-Nisa, verse 1, which couples the fear of Allah with the maintenance of kinship ties.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Washha, from Muhammad Bin Fuzayl Al Sayrafi,

(It has been narrated) from Al Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The kinship of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, the Imams<sup>asws</sup>, would attach with the Throne saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Maintain Relationship with the one who maintained (relationship with) me, and Cut off the one who cut me off’.
Then if flows, after it, in the relationships of the Believers’.
Then heasws recited this Verse [4:1] and fear Allah, by Whom you are asking by Him and the kinship’.
en.sarwar: 26. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Washsha’ from Muhammad ibn Fudayl al-Sayrafi from al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The kindred relation of the family of Muhammad, the A ’immah (people who possess Divine Authority), recipients of divine supreme covenant, holds to the Throne (of the Lord) and says, ‘O Lord establish good relations with those who establish good relations with me and cut off with those who cut off with me. ’
Thereafter it is applicable to the kindred relations of the believers.
The Imam then read this verse: ‘Have fear of the One by whose name you swear to settle your differences and have respect for your relatives. . . [4:1]
